Complete every panel by row-then-column closure and output one panel-sized grid, painting 8 wherever at least two completed rectangles overlap.

review_brief:
# Review: 8e52225f35b8

Built the complete native `closure_order` family while preserving the canonical row→column program byte-for-byte. The alternate changes only the stateful composition to column→row. Two demonstrations uniquely identify either setting; all episodes retain four distinct queries, and demo-count changes preserve the same query bank.

Adversarial attacks covered wrong order, one-axis/partial closure, per-panel bounding boxes, all-panel intersection, global closure, raw-mark majority, memorized first-demo masks, matched-setting controls, orientation controls, malformed numeric/grid types, count boundaries, duplicate inputs, corrupt labels, stale programs, forged certificates, and private/future-query leakage.

Two concrete defects were found and repaired: the base easy band's two panels collapsed majority into all-panel intersection, and some initial 30×30 seeds used only 22 non-separator columns. Final ordinary base draws use 3–4 panels with exactly-two overlap; final stress scenes use at least 25/27 panel columns, all 30 rows, and 27 marks.

Final source passed nine focused tests, a 24-episode bounded probe with 118 protected-Racket evaluations, native authoring preflight at two demos, protected causal replay, 16-view sequential export verification, 24 first-turn invariance mutations, and changed-target tests. This finite evidence does not prove universal uniqueness; owner qualification, acceptance, and training admission remain pending.

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid split into K (2-4) same-size panels by full-height color-9 divider columns. Each panel holds a color-2 rectangle (drawn as 4 corner marks; the rule double-closes them into a filled rectangle). Output is one panel size, marking 8 where a cell lies inside >= 2 panels' rectangles. Panel size, count and the per-panel rectangles all vary.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

parametric_work.limits: Finite reviewer evidence over six adversarial seeds and preflight seeds 0/17; no claim of universal semantic uniqueness, owner acceptance, or training admission.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: Three panel-local, input-dependent first-stage closure masks.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Within each panel, close the marked cells along the episode-selected first axis (rows for row_then_column; columns for column_then_row).
sequential_dependency.step_b: Close each first-stage mask along the other axis, align the panel masks, count per-cell coverage, and paint cyan where at least two panels cover the cell.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The second-axis spans and the final majority counts are computed from cells created by step A; changing the first closure changes which cells step B can span and changes the final cyan mask.

parametric_work.summary: Reviewer-ready native family: exact canonical row-then-column default plus column-then-row alternate on matched inputs; 2-6 demonstrations, exactly four queries, final source inventory, protected authoring preflight, sequential export checks, and protected causal replay all pass. Owner qualification, acceptance, and training admission remain pending.

target_report.summary: Repaired the base's two-panel majority shortcut and built a source-bound native closure-order family with a two-demo minimum, four distinct queries, substantive 30x30 coverage, strict privacy/contract checks, protected-Racket qualification, and a causal order witness.
